definitions.known_boundary: Under the standard finite simple-graph reading, current full texts still leave exactly the even degrees 4,6,...,22 open; Thomason excludes every odd degree and Haxell-Seamone-Verstraete exclude all r>22. Fleischner's simple constructions and Brinkmann-De Pauw Theorem 3.11 realize mixed degree sets, not a singleton regular degree; their Corollary 3.14 and Fleischner's earlier construction give even-regular examples only as multigraphs. Zamfirescu's regular examples have a unique longest, generally nonspanning cycle, and Pitz's uniquely Hamiltonian cubic examples are infinite Hamilton-circle examples. No checked source supplies a finite simple r-regular uniquely Hamiltonian graph or closes the remaining simple cases.
